text:
The evidence can't tell us what caused the 2022 loss. It shows that it happened, but not why.

What it does show: Hansen/UMD mapped about 0.6 ha of tree-cover loss in 2022 within ASSET-I (3.41% of the 17.6 ha). The JRC 2020 reference map agrees that the whole area was forest in 2020. The Uruguayan forest map (MGAP 2021) classes about 0.5 ha as native forest and 0.1 ha as outside mapped forest, with no planted forest. A later year was also observed, which corroborates the loss. A further 0.2 ha of smaller patch loss is not counted as an event.

What it does not show: Hansen loss covers any stand replacement, so it doesn't establish deforestation or land-use change. It also can't distinguish harvest, fire, storm or clearing. Nor does it speak to legality, responsibility or compliance (e.g., EUDR status).

Determining the cause would need other evidence, such as field checks, permit records or higher-resolution imagery.
